findings.claim: The new early return skips every generic type with no syntax, including closed generic classes and other metadata generics, and the ledger records no decision about this. Previously only the struct/record struct case crashed. L8 says types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed, which supports skipping the diagnostics. L11-L13 give no preference on whether the consuming resolver should include a formatter for the closed type, and say to follow the requirement, which expects a generated resolver. This looks consistent with L8, so it is recorded as checked rather than as a defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly; [L11]-[L13] follow the requirement.

findings.claim: The README and MsgPack004 docs state that diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining assembly. This matches the L8 convention and is not a defect. However, the README sentence says closed generic types from referenced assemblies can be used as members, without saying that the consuming assembly generates no formatter for them. Readers may expect a formatter, and trimmed or NativeAOT use then depends on the defining assembly's resolver.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] the defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types; the docs are consistent with it.

findings.claim: The new generic early return and the ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter on all reported diagnostics change analyzer behaviour broadly. Any diagnostic whose location is null or not in the compilation is now silently dropped, which includes cases that were not crashes. L10 warns that analyzer diagnostics have been adjusted for false positives and that changes can cause wrong reports. A diagnostic created with a null location, such as the MemberNeedsKey fallback, is now silently suppressed.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005/etc.) and add a case where a diagnostic is created with Location.None to confirm it is still reported when expected.
